text: Inlined code drops the runtime's checks, so programs behave differently at -O0 and -O2 and can access out of bounds. fir.if plus a call has no data dependence on the protected op, unknown memory effects that block alias-based optimizations, and no noreturn. cf.assert writes the default resource and lowers to puts/abort instead of the Fortran runtime's message. Guarded results are consumed by the protected ops, so SSA dominance enforces the order (flang/docs/InlineRuntimeChecks.md).
